note: Removal records for tools/rooting/retire_check.py rules M1-M4 (AGENTS.md section 10, failure register row 'Consolidation lost files': a removal is a migration or an authorized retirement; name the replacement or the retained obligation, inventory affected consumers, and gate reachability; no bare rm). SCHEMA. Top level: schema (1), note (this text), rules (the M1-M4 id/title/description triples the gate prints under --list), removals (the records), self_test (the synthetic tree, the accepted fixture registry and one seeded defect per rejected record, so --self-test and --controls need no network, clock, Lean or Rust). Each record: id (nonempty, unique, the key every diagnostic names); kind ('migration' | 'retirement'); removed (repo-relative paths the removal deleted, recorded for the receipt - absence is not gated here, R1 gates the binned route); replacement (repo-relative paths that take over the removed ones; empty for a retirement); retained_obligation (what stays open instead of a replacement; empty for a migration); consumers (nonempty repo-relative inventory of what consumed the removed paths - every entry must resolve); reachability (nonempty list of {cwd, argv}; cwd is a repo-relative directory that must resolve, argv is the exact command, argv[0] must resolve as a path under cwd or as a program on the ambient PATH, and every later repo-relative file token in argv must resolve); receipt (nonempty discharge receipt: either a docs/evidence/ledger.jsonl id or the repo-relative path of the governing document that authorizes the removal - it is resolved, so an id the ledger does not carry and a path absent from the tree are both refused). Rules: M1 refuses a record naming neither replacement nor retained obligation; M2 refuses an empty consumer inventory or a consumer path that does not resolve; M3 refuses reachability evidence naming no command, or a command whose cwd, argv[0] or repo-relative file token does not resolve; M4 refuses a deletion record carrying no receipt id, or a receipt that resolves to nothing. Structure is strict (a nonobject record, a duplicate id, a bad kind or a wrong field type is a data error, exit 2); content is what M1-M4 refuse (exit 1). Resolution is existence, not correctness: a ledger row is read for its id only, and no command is run, so a record whose program is not installed on the PATH that runs the gate is refused there.

rules.title: Removal names no replacement and no retained obligation
rules.description: A record in tools/rooting/removals.json has an empty replacement list and an empty retained_obligation: nothing takes over the removed paths and nothing is recorded as staying open, so the removal is neither a migration nor an authorized retirement.

rules.title: Consumer inventory empty or unresolvable
rules.description: A removal record carries no consumers, or names a consumer path that does not resolve under the repository root, so the affected consumers were never inventoried.

rules.title: Reachability evidence absent or unresolvable
rules.description: A removal record names no reachability command, or names a command whose cwd is not a directory in the tree, whose argv[0] resolves neither as a path under that cwd nor as a program on PATH, or whose later repo-relative file token does not resolve. The program is resolved, not run: PATH is the ambient one, so a record naming a program this machine does not install is refused here.

rules.title: Bare deletion record or unresolvable receipt
rules.description: A removal record carries no receipt id, so the deletion is a bare rm with no discharge receipt, or names a receipt that resolves to no docs/evidence/ledger.jsonl id and to no file in the tree. The receipt is a ledger id or the repo-relative path of the authorizing document, and it must resolve.
